text:
mika: throwing up a short proposal — Burst Admission Policy v0. Goal: predictable short bursts for reserved pools without increasing platform risk. Idea: use a dual-threshold model (committed quota + elastic buffer) with exponential decay on buffer consumption. Want quick alignment on metrics, billing, and canary plan.

frank: dual-threshold sounds promising. How is elastic buffer different from previous headroom ideas?

mika: buffer is explicit per-tenant seconds (not %). It decays as you spend it (e.g., half-life), so sustained usage is naturally discouraged. Buffer is tracked in a small ledger and can be granted free for pilots or sold as add-on.

zoe: infra note: ledger must be readable very cheaply at router time. Recommend a compact in-memory cache + fallback to Redis for cold tenants. Prefer a single integer (remaining_ms) per tenant to reduce hot-key issues.

harry: billing/commercial Q: free vs paid buffer? sales prefers a small free baseline (e.g., 30s/day) and overage billed at a predictable surge rate. Legal wants clear wording around bursts vs committed SLA.

mika: proposal for alpha defaults: free_buffer_daily=30s, buffer_max=300s, decay_half_life=1h, billing_rate=0.5x for pilot. Opt-in pilot.

frank: router behavior sketch: 1) if under committed quota: normal. 2) if over and buffer>0: allow and tag request header X-Burst-Buffer=true and decrement buffer. 3) if buffer exhausted -> follow preempt/autoscale. Make buffer check O(1) and lock-free where possible.

zoe: concurrency concerns: when many requests consume buffer simultaneously we need atomic decrement. Use sharded counters per-tenant to avoid contention and occasional negative reads are OK — we'll reconcile in billing.

harry: metrics to capture for launch:
- buffer_balance (time series)
- buffer_consumed_rate
- spillover_to_autoscale_count
- cross-tenant latency delta when buffers in use

mika: acceptance criteria suggestion:
- pilot with 3 tenants (varied sizes)
- no 99.9p latency regression >12% for non-bursting tenants over 2 weeks
- billing export matches ledger within 98% in staging for 7 days

frank: dev checklist:
- small ledger service (accrue/consume/get_balance) with TTL-backed rows
- router hook + header propagation
- tracing tags: burst.buffer.allow, burst.buffer.exhausted, burst.buffer.reconciled
- global conservative cap to avoid platform oversubscribe

zoe: ops items:
- add alert: regional_buffer_usage > 50% for 10m -> ops page
- retention: buffer events 30d for billing, aggregated 365d for audit
- FF per-tenant + global kill switch

harry: billing CSV fields required: tenant_id, ts_start, ts_end, buffer_seconds_used, cost_usd, pilot_flag. Finance wants a sample CSV before pilot starts.

mika: canary plan: enable in staging, run synthetic microbursts, then internal single-tenant canary, then 3-customer pilot behind flags. Collect metrics for 14 days before GA decision.

frank: risk log entries to RFC:
- customer surprise on bills if not communicated well
- noisy neighbor if global cap mis-set
- edge-case: buffer spend during quota change (upgrade/downgrade) — need clear calc rule

zoe: implementation detail: when quota changes, scale remaining buffer proportionally to new committed rate and log the event for audit. Put exact formula in RFC.

harry: customer messaging: sales one-pager + console banner + invoice line item. Pilot opt-in only. Legal to review phrasing.

product-bot: created channel #pilot-burst-buffer-1767778888 and scheduled a reminder Thu 11:00 to review pilot metrics.

mika: next steps: I'll draft a short RFC with data model, buffer math, and the billing CSV schema. frank/zoe to prototype ledger pattern. harry to coordinate pilot comms. Target RFC review in 4 business days. Thanks! :rocket:
